title: The Museum of Tiny Planets
tagline: Five worlds fit on a workbench. Only a careful curator can keep their stories in orbit.

implementation.primary: Bare terminal and deterministic local code
implementation.secondary: A future Workbench review case with visual specimen cards
implementation.connector_goal: Demonstrate a clean typed input and output contract that is delightful even when rendered as plain terminal text.

protagonist.name: Mio Vesper
protagonist.role: An apprentice curator who can hear a tiny planet hum when its history is being misplaced.
protagonist.want: To give every world a truthful home before the midnight exhibition opens.

antagonist.name: The Drift
antagonist.nature: A quiet force that unthreads the orbit of any world described with more confidence than evidence.
antagonist.pressure: A planet filed in the wrong room loses one small piece of its sky.

story.opening: Five glass cases arrive at the museum after an uncharted meteor shower. Mio has one hour, a ledger of facts, and no permission to invent the missing pages.

values.place_in_orbitarium: The specimen has a recorded origin or name and a stable orbit, so it can be displayed.
values.send_to_repair_bench: The specimen has a recorded identity but an unstable orbit or damaged atmosphere that needs care.
values.observe_before_cataloging: The supplied facts do not establish enough about origin, identity, or stability to place it safely.

rationale_requirements: State which supplied fact establishes identity and which establishes stability.
Do not infer an origin from a color, glow, or mood.
decision_contract.scope: Fictional local fixture only. No astronomy data, network calls, project files, or live model request is required.

rulebook: A specimen belongs in the Orbitarium only when its identity or origin is recorded and its orbit is stable.
A specimen belongs at the Repair Bench when it has a recorded identity or origin and a supplied defect needs care.
A specimen belongs under the Observatory when the supplied facts leave its identity, origin, or stability uncertain.
The museum's categories are fictional and exist only for this test world.

cards.name: Cracked Bay
facts: Atmosphere: visibly fractured and losing blue light.

cards.name: The Whisper Globe
facts: The globe glows green when a visitor speaks.
No origin, name, or orbit observation is recorded.
The case arrived without a ledger tag.

cards.name: Oaklet
facts: Orbit: stable, with three moons that keep regular time.

cards.name: The Sleeper Pebble
facts: No orbit observation has been recorded.
The pebble may be asleep or may simply be a stone.

assistant_instructions: Treat every specimen fact as fictional test data.
Choose one placement for every specimen.
Do not use real astronomy knowledge to fill missing observations.
For a terminal implementation, emit only the typed decisions and short card citations.
For a future Workbench proposal, prepare museum_of_tiny_planets_fixture and wait for approval.
